fact: Green iguanas are strong climbers and have long tails that help with balance.
Marine iguanas are the only modern lizards that regularly feed in the ocean.
Chameleons can move their eyes independently and shoot out long sticky tongues.
Panther chameleons can display many bright color patterns.
Bearded dragons can puff up the spiny skin under their throats.
Komodo dragons are the largest living lizards.
Gila monsters are venomous lizards that store fat in their thick tails.
Leopard geckos have movable eyelids and can shed their tails to escape danger.
Crested geckos have ridges above their eyes that look like tiny eyelashes.
Tokay geckos are large colorful geckos known for loud calls.
Blue-tongued skinks flash their bright blue tongues when threatened.
Green anoles can change between green and brown shades.
Frilled lizards can spread a large skin frill around their necks.
Basilisk lizards can sprint across the surface of water for short distances.
Thorny devils are covered in spikes and collect moisture between the scales of their skin.
Monitor lizards are active hunters with long necks, strong tails, and forked tongues.
Corn snakes are nonvenomous snakes that kill prey by constriction.
Ball pythons may curl into a tight ball when frightened.
King cobras are the longest venomous snakes in the world.
Rattlesnakes shake special tail segments to make a warning buzz.
Boa constrictors wrap their muscular bodies around prey.
Green anacondas are among the heaviest snakes in the world.
Garter snakes are widespread snakes that often live near gardens and wetlands.
Milk snakes are nonvenomous and often have bold bands of red, black, and pale colors.
Hognose snakes have upturned snouts that help them dig in loose soil.
Black mambas are fast venomous snakes native to parts of Africa.
Reticulated pythons are among the longest snakes in the world.
Sea snakes have flattened tails that help them swim.
Nile crocodiles are powerful predators that live in African rivers and lakes.
American alligators build nests from plants and mud.
Gharials have very long narrow snouts adapted for catching fish.
Spectacled caimans get their name from a raised ridge between their eyes.
Green sea turtles migrate long distances between feeding and nesting areas.
Loggerheads have large heads and strong jaws that can crush hard-shelled prey.
Leatherbacks are the largest sea turtles and have flexible leathery shells.
Red-eared sliders are named for the red patches behind their eyes.
Box turtles can close their hinged lower shells tightly for protection.
Snapping turtles have strong jaws and long tails.
Galápagos tortoises can live for well over a century.
African spurred tortoises are large desert tortoises that dig deep burrows.
Some poison dart frogs get defensive chemicals from the foods they eat in the wild.
Tree frogs have toe pads that help them cling to leaves and branches.
Bullfrogs are large frogs with deep calls that can carry across ponds.
Many glass frogs have partly transparent skin on their undersides.
Red-eyed tree frogs have bright red eyes and sticky toe pads.
Tomato frogs can puff up their round bodies when threatened.
Horned frogs have wide mouths and sit quietly while waiting for prey.
Leopard frogs are named for the dark spots across their backs and legs.
Toads have bumpy skin and produce defensive chemicals from glands behind their eyes.
Cane toads are large toads with strong defensive glands.
Fire-bellied toads show bright belly colors as a warning to predators.
Axolotls keep their feathery external gills as adults.
Tiger salamanders spend much of their lives hidden underground.
Fire salamanders have striking yellow markings on dark skin.
Eastern newts have a bright orange juvenile stage called a red eft.
Olms are pale cave-dwelling amphibians that can live in complete darkness.
Mudpuppies are aquatic salamanders that keep external gills throughout life.
Caecilians are limbless amphibians that look a little like large worms.
Sirens are eel-shaped amphibians with tiny front legs and no hind legs.
Hellbenders are giant aquatic salamanders that hide beneath rocks in cool streams.
